title: Propeller Pitch System
description: The pitch linkage as five rigid bodies and their joints, with the two end stops, at 72 degrees blade pitch; no tolerances yet. Model v2; v1 is the legacy whole-system model.

provenance.structure_source: Jeff's forge note 20261108T001814_kpoev0 (2026-11-08): 'a new, simpler version of the model, focusing on just the kinematic end stop tolerance', each rigid body a chained stack, 'a single blade, pitch link, and tangential link to start out', and every correct 3D body including the piston cover.
provenance.joints_source: The P2 linkage sweep, data/inbox/linkage-sweeps/vpa-pitch-p2-20261105-204957.json: its geometry.features name ten of this document's nodes by body, under v1's ids, which is why every id here that v1 has is v1's.
provenance.ids: Every node id and every edge id v1 (`vpa_pitch_linkage`) also has names the same feature there; `ids_from` declares it (docs/DAG_TOPOLOGY.md, "Models").

bodies.name: ground
bodies.note: The hub, the two mounts and the piston cover, as a stack: the tangential link mount seats on the hub, the gas-spring mount on the tangential link mount (`tan_link_mount_gas_spring_seat`; Jeff, 2026-11-10: 'mount on mount'), and the piston cover's flange on the gas-spring mount (`piston_cover_mount_flange_seat`). Each of the three joints is a seat, a locating boss in a bore and a fastener pattern (Jeff, 2026-11-10: 'the same datum style with a flange, central locating boss, and fastener pattern for clocking'). linkage's base lists the first three parts alone; the difference is declared beside the pairing test.

bodies.name: tangential link
bodies.note: The machined link 213863-004 and its two bearings' outer races, swaged into its bores (Jeff's note 20261119T142516_ci28ci; handoff a_link_is_a_machined_part_and_two_bearings_each_two_races, 2026-11-19). The 212956-005 assembly and its two bearings are in no body: each bearing's inner race moves with the part it is fixed to. linkage lists the assembly alone, because its mesh draws all of it -- the difference is declared beside the pairing test.

bodies.name: pitch plate
bodies.note: The plate assembly (the plate and its two flanged bushings), the two straight bushings, the gas-spring piston and the two piston heads. The two piston heads are the plate's: the lower sits on the piston body's shoulder (`piston_body_head_seat`) and the upper stacks on it (`piston_heads_seat`). The plate seats and is bolted on the piston body's flange about its pilot boss; one spigot on the piston body locates both heads, and the upper head is bolted to the piston body through the lower head's bore (2026-11-17, read off the meshes). linkage's pitch plate lists the first two parts alone; the difference is declared beside the pairing test.

bodies.name: pitch link
bodies.note: The machined link 213861-002 and its two bearings' outer races, swaged into its bores (Jeff's note 20261119T142516_ci28ci; handoff a_link_is_a_machined_part_and_two_bearings_each_two_races, 2026-11-19). The 213862-002 assembly and its two MS14101-3 bearings are in no body: each bearing's inner race moves with the part it is fixed to. A two-force member: the distance between the two outer races' centres is the assembly's one length. The bearings' tolerances come from their datasheet (Jeff).

bodies.name: blade 1
bodies.note: Blade 1 and its pitch arm: the arm's ring seats on the blade root's fitting, on its boss, clocked by one radial hole through both (2026-11-17, read off the meshes).

nodes.name: locating boss
nodes.note: Concentric by design with the main bearings the whole propeller turns on; those bearings and the shaft are not in this model.

nodes.name: blade 1 root bearing bore
nodes.note: The blade turns in this bore about its pitch axis: the base's rotary joint with the blade.

nodes.name: pilot bore
nodes.note: The bore that locates the mount radially on the hub's circular boss.

nodes.name: tangential link mount fastener pattern
nodes.note: The ring of fasteners round the mount's flange through matching holes constrains its rotation about the boss. One node on both parts, as v1's `pitch_arm_blade_root_clocking`.

nodes.name: gas-spring mount base face
nodes.note: The gas-spring mount's base face, its datum A, seated on the tangential link mount: mount on mount, with no seat on the hub.

nodes.name: locating boss
nodes.note: The spigot under the gas-spring mount's base face that locates it radially in the tangential link mount. On the 213668 mesh (`machined_213668`): two lands of one boss, faces 73/622 (z 126.55 to 127.55) and 81/624 (z 132.50 to 133.50), both diameter 220.370, with a 214.782 relief between. The mount carries the boss here, the opposite of the hub joint below it. Every mesh named here places its part at the identity, so the numbers are in the assembly frame; a measurement of a mesh, never a value.

nodes.name: pitch arm clocking holes
nodes.note: The hole through the pitch arm's ring into the blade root that fixes the arm's rotation about the blade's pitch axis. A fastener pattern, as in v1, which uses the same id. notes: Studyless by design for now: M2 adds one term per body and the end-stop study over them (dispatch/docs/strategy/drafts/DRAFT_tolerance_analysis_over_the_kinematic_model.md, '2026-11-08 -- the reset').
No edge carries a dimension. Each says what would close it; an untraced zero would read as a measured one.

Left out, on purpose: the gas spring, the VPA and its piston, the ring gear, the hydraulic brake, every fastener and washer, every bushing but the four at the pitch link's and the tangential link's plate attachments, and blades 2 to 5. v1 keeps all of them.

Named once, 2026-11-10 (handoff the_model_is_derived_once_and_the_left_column_is_its_tree): a feature's name says the feature and not the part it is nested under; a feature two parts share names the seated part; a dimension is <from> to <to> in those words; one spelling of each term (locating boss, end stop, tangential link).

Edge order, 2026-11-10 (handoff the_gas_spring_mount_sits_on_the_tan_link_mount_in_the_end_stop_model): the walk is authored, and the hub's edges read its joint with the tangential link mount before its blade bore, so the base reads up the stack from the hub. With the blade bore first the parts drawn as blocks crossed once more than the builder's walk.

Each link, 2026-11-19 (handoff a_link_is_a_machined_part_and_two_bearings_each_two_races, 2026-11-19): a machined part and two spherical bearings, each bearing an outer race swaged into the machined part and an inner race fixed to the part the link attaches to, joined by one spherical gap edge. The link's body is the machined part and its outer races; each inner race is in its mating part's body; the link assembly and the bearings are in none. The four sphere centres keep v1's ids on the outer races; v1's four joint edges are not in this model.
